title: Imagination as a Moderator of the Relationship between Screen Time and Resistance to Using Digital Devices in Children 6–7 Years Old
abstract: Today's preschoolers are experiencing increased screen time and new behavioral phenomena, including resistance to stopping digital device use (negative emotions, protest, and affective outbursts). Despite evidence linking screen time to emotional and behavioral difficulties in children, the psychological factors that may weaken or strengthen this association remain insufficiently studied. Imagination, as a key mental function of preschool age, may serve as an internal resource facilitating the child's transition to alternative activities. The aim of this study was to assess the role of imagination as a moderator of the relationship between screen time and a child's resistance to discontinuing the use of digital devices. Methods. The study involved 350 preschool children (ages 6-7 years) attending kindergartens in Moscow, Kazan, Perm, and Yakutsk. Data on the duration of screen time and the occurrence of resistance upon discontinuing the use of digital devices were obtained through a survey of mothers. Imagination was assessed using O. M. Dyachenko's "Figure Completion" method, which evaluates the originality, flexibility, elaboration, and coefficient of originality of imagination. Descriptive statistics, the Mann-Whitney U test, and moderation analysis were employed for data analysis. Results. Resistance to discontinuing the use of digital devices was observed in the majority of children. Boys exhibited longer screen time duration, whereas girls demonstrated higher levels of imagination development. Moderation analysis revealed that the elaboration of imagination is a significant moderator of the relationship between active screen time on weekdays and the occurrence of resistance in girls. At low levels of imagination elaboration, an increase in active screen time was associated with a higher probability of resistance upon discontinuing device use. No statistically significant effects were found for other indicators of imagination or for the subsample of boys. Conclusions. A developed imagination can be an important internal resource, facilitating a child's successful transition from digital activities to alternative pursuits. The development of imagination can be considered one of the factors in the psychological adaptation of preschoolers to the digital environment.
